name: manifest-dev
description: Manifest-driven development: /figure-out reaches shared understanding, /define writes Deliverables with Acceptance Criteria and Global Invariants, and /do implements them. Each gate is one text — a title, a body, and an optional why — carrying a required kind (judgment or deterministic, never inferred) as its only structured metadata; execution policy is selected at /do launch as per-gate (independent default), consolidated, or self, with an optional verifier model for independent modes. Every mode keeps a provenance-rich gate ledger and the run never downgrades itself. Re-verification follows each gate's declared kind: command-backed gates re-run in full, while judgment gates take one full look and then judge only prior findings' repairs and the changed delta, with --exhaustive-verification restoring full re-sampling. A default-on execution log preserves deviations and dead-end memory; --no-log opts out. For unattended runs, use a host-native goal-setting backstop whose completion contract requires fresh PASS evidence for every gate under the selected mode. /auto chains the full flow, and /figure-out-team extends deliberation to multi-party Slack sessions. /ticket-up authors convention-compliant Tickets from a Manifest, direct work, independently managed questions, or source-linked follow-ups; one Manifest becomes one coherent Shaped Ticket by default, with Deliverable splitting reserved for explicit delegation, and follow-up Auto granted only when both source authority and the follow-up's own grant hold. /next-ticket claims and presents the top ready Ticket without executing it. /run-ticket receives one exact Ticket from a person or trigger, invokes /auto without enforcing Auto or selecting backlog work, and records DONE or ESCALATED evidence on that same Ticket. Stores use the project's shared tracker, GitHub Issues out of the box, or files where cross-checkout claiming is not needed. /init-context sets a repository up with the surfaces the workflow reads from — project-owned ADR conventions, a glossary, and the context-file wiring that keeps sessions using them — seeding them from the project's own history where there is any.
